Q: JVM version manager A:

Jolta is a new version manager for Java and it is by far the best.
Just visit https://oneappplatform.github.io/jolta/ and do the one line terminal install, and you will never have to manually install or switch java versions again.

It handles download-on-demand, even on a system that has never had java before. You can pin a specific version of java to a directory and it uses that. You can supply a JVM vendor preference. There are a ton of features, but its best feature is if you want to, you can install it once and totally forget about it.

It seamlessly works in the background resolving your $JAVA_HOME properly.

Give it a try!

Q: Programmatically add qdiscs and filters using either netlink or iproute2 A:

iproute2 doesn't ship a library you can link against, that's the wall you're hitting. tc_qdisc_modify and the rest are static code inside the tc binary, never meant to be called from outside, so there's no header or package to include and pulling tc's .c files in drags half of iproute2's internal plumbing with them.

Two ways people actually do this.

libnl, the libnl-route part specifically, wraps exactly this. Allocate a qdisc, set its kind and params, add it:

struct rtnl_qdisc *qdisc = rtnl_qdisc_alloc();
rtnl_tc_set_link(TC_CAST(qdisc), link);
rtnl_tc_set_kind(TC_CAST(qdisc), "htb");
rtnl_qdisc_add(sock, qdisc, NLM_F_CREATE);

filters are the rtnl_cls_* family, same shape. Link with pkg-config --libs libnl-route-3.0. This is what I'd reach for unless you've got a reason to avoid the dependency.

Raw rtnetlink if you want zero deps. Open an AF_NETLINK socket with NETLINK_ROUTE and send an RTM_NEWQDISC message: an nlmsghdr, a struct tcmsg (tcm_ifindex, tcm_parent, tcm_handle), a TCA_KIND attribute with the qdisc name, and a nested TCA_OPTIONS holding that qdisc's own config. RTM_NEWTFILTER for filters. More code, and the attribute nesting is where it gets fiddly.

Fastest way to nail the exact bytes for whatever qdisc you're building: run the tc command you already know works under strace and read the message it sends.

strace -e trace=sendmsg -s 4096 tc qdisc add dev eth0 root htb

that sendmsg buffer is the RTM_NEWQDISC you need to reconstruct, params and all. I got a couple of qdiscs working that way faster than reading the netlink docs.

Q: What is the correct way to register a CNG provider (Key Storage Provider/KSP) on ARM64? A:

I was able to test that I can dynamically open bcrypt.dll on ARM64 and call the BCryptREgisterProvider() and BCryptUnregisterPRovider() functions without any issue.

Q: store return value of a Python script in a bash script A:

The purpose of sys.exit() is to return an integer code indicating whether your program succeeded or not--0 means success, any other number means failure. Therefore, it's probably not ideal for returning a file path in your instance.

Instead, use a simple Python print() to return the output of your script. Then, you can catch the code that you printed using Bash's $() syntax, like so:

In the Python script, write:

print(myString)

And then in the Bash script, write:

outputString=$(python myPythonScript arg1 arg2 arg3)

If you need to print other things to Terminal, but don't want the Bash script catching them, you can print them to stderr instead of stdout. For more on the difference between stdout, stderr, and stdin, see this post.

Hope this helps!
